title: Leaving New Orleans for Chicago in 1926
summary: Williams says he moved to Chicago at 19; his father, a contractor, could not get into the union and went back, as did his mother in the 1930s. He travelled free on the railroad.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

In the 30s? Yeah. And you stayed here in Chicago all the time? Oh, I thought, yeah. You only went back to New Orleans for some days. Business? Yeah. Oh, yeah.
